about: The shared surfaces fixture (m3-design section 4; briefs M3-06 and M3-10), the seam between the pipeline's surfaces step and the game's SurfaceGrid. tests/shared/surfaces_fixture/ holds a synthetic world (world.json: origin E 2700000 / N 1200000, height_offset_m 750.0, the owner's axes, area 'fixture' E 2700012-2700052, N 1199971-1200001: 40 m x 30 m, so x 12 ... 52 and z -1 ... 29) and source.json: a synthetic swissTLM3D (invented features, UUIDs and codes; no swisstopo data) in the reader's form, coordinates in whole millimetres, layers as the FileGDB holds them (not in UUID order). The reader hands over the features whose geometry meets the area box grown by 10 m (listed in 'read', sorted by UUID): not the L-shaped stream whose bounding box meets that box but whose line stays 15 m away, not a road 30 m east, not a rock annulus whose hole holds the whole box, not a path 0.5 m outside the grown box; but the path that touches the grown box at one point and the Wald polygon that encloses it. The class grid at 0.2 m (200 columns x 150 rows, rows north to south) covers every class and priority (road > path > water > rock > none), a tunnel, a gallery, an Unterfuehrung, a road in/auf Gebaeude, a Platz, a Klettersteig and an unknown surface not drawn, a bridge and a Treppe drawn, a 1 m Weg with a hard surface as road and a 3 m Strasse with a natural surface as path, the 2m Wegfragment (18) and 8m Strasse (20) widths, a rock polygon with a hole and one overlapping it, a waterfall drawn and an underground stream, a stream on a bridge, a Trockenrinne and a Bisse not drawn, features outside the area that reach into it, a line of two parts with a gap, a repeated vertex, and ties on purpose: polygon edges through texel centres (half-open: west and south edges in, east and north out), a vertex on a centre, centres at exactly half a width from a segment and from a segment's end. Expected outputs were computed two independent ways (a vectorised numpy implementation and a pure-Python row scanline with Fractions; identical bytes) at 0.2, 0.5 and 1 m; generated/ holds the 0.2 m output: the PNG (8-bit greyscale, filter 0 on every row, one zlib stream at level 9 in IDAT chunks of at most 1 MiB; its bytes depend on the zlib build, so only its pixels are pinned), its keep-file import note and its description, and a manifest whose other blocks are null. 'points' name texel centres (and four points 0.04 m from a texel boundary) with their class; the game finds each at class_at(local x, z) and each local point is WorldConfig.to_local of its LV95 point; 'outside' points give -1. 'twins' records, for the likeliest wrong implementations, how many texels differ and which points catch them.
